terms.comment: The ordinary word; a female slave is ancilla (serva is rare). Slavery is servitūs, servitūtis f.; to be a slave, servīre.
The usual feminine of servus (Lewis & Short); in later and modern Latin a maidservant.
A legal word: first the formal purchase by taking in hand, then the slave so bought; it treats the person as a thing owned.

phrases.latin: ‘servī sunt.’ immō hominēs. ‘servī sunt.’ immō contubernālēs. ‘servī sunt.’ immō humilēs amīcī
phrases.english: ‘They are slaves.’ No, they are people. ‘They are slaves.’ No, they share our roof. ‘They are slaves.’ No, they are humble friends.

phrases.latin: Ulixēs domī etiam contumēliās servōrum ancillārumque pertulit
phrases.english: at home Ulysses even put up with the insults of the slaves and the maids
